en: Extraction of the Mantra.
Homage to the Buddha.
Showing the sequential order of the means for accomplishment (*sādhanopāyikā*) of the *Śrī-Guhyasamāja-mahāyoga-tantra*, he says:
"First is the retention of the mantra; second is the instruction on the placement [of the syllables]."
The third is the establishment of order, and the fourth is the vision of reality.
Thus [it is said].
The meaning of this sūtra is as follows: first of all, the entire mantra-word is the means of accomplishment (sādhana).
Having extracted [the mantra] from the root and planted it within the mind, one should ascertain it;
thus, the ascertainment of the mantra comes first.
Thereafter, within the aggregates, elements, sense-bases, and so forth, [one should contemplate them] in the form of Vairocana and the other [deities].
"One should place [the deities] upon one's own body-maṇḍala"—
this is the second teaching on placement (nyāsa).
Regarding each of the deities thus placed, their respective individual characteristics [are to be visualized] in successive order.
Having fully understood and described the wheel of deities (*devatācakra*), the third stage is established.
Having unified [the mind] through subtle yoga, one should deposit the mantras by means of entry, abiding, and emergence; this is the fourth reality (*tattva*).
The vision.
Now the mantra for seizing by means of mantras is written: Vajradhṛk!
Hūṃ! Oṃ sumbha nisumbha hūṃ, gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ, gṛhṇāpaya gṛhṇāpaya.

Phaṭ 2! Kīlaya 2 all evils, phaṭ 2! Hūṃ 2! Vajrakīla, the Holder of the Vajra commands the bodies of all obstructors!
Nail down the vajra of speech and mind! Hūṃ 2 Phaṭ 2! Ṭakki hūṃ jaḥ!
Hūṃ! Bhrūṃ! Oṃ āḥ hūṃ!
By this, the visualization of the protection wheel is established.
In the absence of existence, there is no cultivation; cultivation is not indeed cultivation.
Thus, existence would not be existence, for cultivation is not perceived.
Having that which is without intrinsic nature as its object.

Hūṃ! The accomplishment of the four mandalas.
Bhrūṃ!
The completion of the peaked pavilion.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra of the wisdom of emptiness.
This is the entry into the ultimate maṇḍala.
The lotus of the sun and moon and the garland of the three syllables; at the periphery, the focal point is the lunar mandala.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the dharmadhātu. This is the consolidation.
Thus is the yoga.
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ.
The accomplishment of Mahāvajradhara. The Anuyoga.
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ svāṃ hāa.
This is the entry into the five aggregates.
Delight in delusion, delight in hatred, delight in passion, and delight in the vajra; this is the penetration into the elements.

Yamāntaka, Prajñāntaka, Padmāntaka, Amṛtakuṇḍalin, Acala, Ṭakkirāja,
Nīladaṇḍa, Mahābala, Uṣṇīṣacakravartin, and Niṣumbharāja— these constitute the maṇḍala of one’s own body.
And that which has as its objective support a nature already accomplished: this is *atiyoga*. Oṃ.
By means of this, there is the radiation of the array of Locanā.
The glorious one who bears the Buddha-body, cultivated through the indivisibility of the three vajras,
may today grant me the state of empowerment as the Vajra-Body.
May the Buddhas residing in the ten directions, who are conceived as the indivisibility of the three vajras,
grant me today the state of empowerment, O Vajra-Body holders!
By this, there is a prayer.
May my body also become such as that of all the Buddhas, which is filled with the five aggregates by way of the intrinsic nature of the Buddha-body.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the body-vajra of all Tathāgatas. By this, there is the consecration of the body-vajra. Āḥ.
The Emanation of the Array of Pāṇḍaravāsinī.
(3) Dharma is indeed the glorious path of speech, cultivated as the indivisibility of the three vajras;
may it today grant me the state of empowerment for the Vajra of Speech.
May the Buddhas residing in the ten directions, who are conceived as the indivisibility of the three vajras,
grant me today the state of empowerment, O Vajra of Speech!
By this, there is a prayer.
Just as the speech of Vajradharma is perfected in its expression,
may my speech likewise become like that of a Holder of the Dharma.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the speech-vajra of all Tathāgatas.
By this, one should cultivate the pride of the speech-vajra;
this is the consecration of the speech-vajra.
Hūṃ!
The radiation of the array of Māmakī.
The glorious holder of the mind-vajra, who is meditated upon as the indivisibility of the three vajras,
may today grant me the state of empowerment of the Mind-Vajra-holder.
May the Buddhas residing in the ten directions, who are conceived as the indivisibility of the three vajras,
grant me today the state of empowerment, O Vajra-mind!
By this, there is a prayer:
(4) "That mind which belongs to Samantabhadra, the wise lord of the Guhyakas..."
May my mind also become like that, comparable to Vajradhara.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the mind-vajra of all Tathāgatas.
By this, one should form the pride of the mind-vajra; this is the consecration of the mind-vajra. Oṃ.
"I am of the nature of the vajra-body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
By this, one should cultivate the pride of the Great Vajradhara.
Hūṃ!
By this, there is the focal object of the Samādhisattva.
Having thus brought oneself to completion as Mahāvajradhara, who consists of the three beings, one should perform the consecration of the deity through this sequence:
Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ Svā Hā.
Locanā, Māmakī,
Pāṇḍaravāsinī,
and Samayatārā.
Rūpavajrā, Śabdavajrā, Gandhavajrā, Rasavajrā, Sparśavajrā; Vajravetālī, Aparājitā, Bhṛkuṭī, Viśvavajrī, and Viśvaratnī.
Viśvapadmī, Viśvakarmī,
Gaganavajriṇī, and Dharaṇīndharī— thus is the removal of the state of being an ordinary woman.
Oṃ hūṃ! The consecration of the vajra. Āḥ!
The consecration of the lotus.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra that impassions all Tathāgatas;
this is the empowerment of Ratnasambhava.
HŪṂ | Moving.
(5) PHAṬ | Emission.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra of worship of all Tathāgatas. This is the empowerment of Amoghasiddhi.
The mantra syllables of the Utsarga-maṇḍala are as follows: Vajradhṛk, Jinajik, Ratnadhṛk, Ārolik, Prajñādhṛk, Moharati, Dveṣarati, Rāgarati.
Vajraratī, Rūpavajrā, Śabdavajrā, Gandhavajrā, Rasavajrā, Sparśavajrā, Maitreya,
Kṣitigarbha, Vajrapāṇi, Khagarbha, and Lokeśvara.
Mañjuśrī,
Sarvanivaraṇaviṣkambhin, Samantabhadra, Yamāntakṛt, Prajñāntakṛt, Padmāntakṛt—
Vighnāntakṛt, Acala, Ṭakkirāja, Nīladaṇḍa,
Mahābala,
Uṣṇīṣacakravartin, and Sumbharāja constitute the maṇḍala of renunciation.
The subtle yoga.
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ. This is the recitation of speech.
O Vajra-mind, Lord of the World, protect me within the realm of sentient beings with your delightful passion for the sake of the great purpose;
desire me, O Father, supreme kinsman of all beings!
If you wish to live today, O Lord!
O Vajra-body, you whose embrace is dear to many beings, O Wheel of Buddhas, who perceives the welfare of others for the sake of awakening and the ultimate truth—
desire me with passion, according to the pledge of passion.
If you wish to live today, O Lord!
O Vajravāca, you who are compassionate toward the welfare of all and always engaged in performing deeds for the sake of the world;
O Samantabhadra, desire me with the practice of supreme bliss.
If you wish to live today, O Lord!

O Vajra-Lover, supreme of commitments, for the sake of great benefit, O ornament of the lineage of the Perfectly Awakened Ones, compassionate in equanimity, desire me, a treasury of virtues who have become many jewels!
If you wish to live today, O Lord.
An exhortation for one who has entered into the ultimate truth.
Akṣobhyavajra, great wisdom, Vajradhātu, great enlightened one; O foremost of the three vajras of the three mandalas, speak the secret! Homage be to you!
Vairocana, great purity, peaceful vajra, great delight; you who teach that phenomena are luminous by nature—O Vajra, homage be to you! (7)
O King of Jewels, most profound, stainless as the vajra-space of the sky,
pure by nature and untainted— speak the secret; homage be to you!
O Vajrāmita, Great King, free from conceptual construction, wielder of the space-vajra;
you who have attained the perfection of passion, speak, O Vajra, homage be to you!
O Amoghavajra, perfectly awakened one, fulfiller of all hopes;
born of the nature of purity, O Vajrasattva, homage be to you!
The offering of praise by one who has emerged from meditative absorption due to the power of previous vows.
Hūṃ.
By this, the conclusion of the mantra is indicated.
Thus ends the extraction of mantras for the practice of the stage of generation (*bhavotpattikrama*) in the *Śrī Guhyasamāja Mahāyogatantra*.
This is the work of the venerable Candrakīrti. (8)
